subject: YEAR-TO-YYYY function
notes: CLOSED BY kb/Work PB248, and the row carried TWO reasons for its PARTIAL - both are now answered. cite.py --check 15.100.3 "Argument-3 shall be an integer greater than 1600 and less than 10000" => OK (15.100.3 4). (1) THE INTEGER-NESS HALF - a floating-point argument-3 passed the 15.3 type-6 screen and TryIntegerArg truncated it toward zero. Rejected at bind now, through PicInfo.IsIntegerDescription, with the drift test asserting this position by name against every floating-point Usage member. (2) THE SPURIOUS-REJECT HALF the refuter added - r4 firing on a reference that OMITS argument-3, because the float body filled baseYear = 0 for the 1- and 2-argument forms alike and took the line-123 range branch. That half was already repaired before this landing: CobolIntrinsics.RealArgs.cs carries TWO overloads (YearToYyyyReal(double, double = 50) delegating to the two-argument CobolDate.YearToYyyy, and the three-argument twin), which is the PB65 "omitted-ness is the ARITY, never a value" discipline propagated to the float carrier; the verdict was stale, and PB248 re-measured it at HEAD rather than inheriting it. It is moot for conforming source in any case - no float operand reaches that body any more - and the permissive coercion lane is covered by conformance-test:FloatIntegerArgumentPermissiveTests. The RANGE half was already correct and correctly strict at both bounds (1600 rejected, 1601 admitted, 9999 admitted, 10000 rejected) and is exercised through the shared core by conformance:cases/15.23.3-Argument-rules/pb65_date_windowing.
